h1: Getting permission for outdoor seating at a brewpub
title: Outdoor Seating Permission for a Brewpub | Craft Beer School
desc: What outdoor seating at a brewpub needs: the licensed premises plan, municipal and fire approvals, neighbours and the numbers that make it worth the effort.
teaser: Outdoor tables can add a lot of covers. They can also put your excise licence at risk if the area is not on the approved plan.
standfirst: A terrace, a courtyard or a few tables on the pavement can change a brewpub's evening trade. Serving alcohol on them is another matter. This guide covers the approvals and the questions to settle first.
sections: The licence covers a drawn area, not the building

A brewpub or bar licence is issued for specific premises, usually shown on an approved plan. Serving alcohol outside that drawn boundary, even on your own terrace, can breach the licence. So the first question about outdoor seating is not about furniture. It is whether the outdoor area can be added to the licensed premises. Then comes what the excise department needs to approve it.

Rules vary by state and change. Some states allow open-air or rooftop service with specific conditions. Others are stricter. Ask a licensing consultant to check the current position for your address before you spend on decking and umbrellas.
Who else needs to say yes

Outdoor seating usually involves more than one authority. Depending on the site and the city, expect some combination of:

  • The excise department, for the change to the licensed premises plan.
  • The municipal corporation, especially if any tables sit on a pavement or public land.
  • The fire department, since exits, escape routes and occupancy limits change when you add covers.
  • The landlord or building society, under the lease and any common area rules.

If you are already filing for signage, the same municipal office may handle both. Our guide on signage permission for a brewpub front covers that process.
Count the covers before the cost

Outdoor seating earns its keep through covers. If you add eight tables of four, that is 32 seats. At one and a half turns on a weekend evening that is 48 more guests a night. Multiply by your real average spend per head from the POS, not a hoped-for one. Then multiply by the number of usable nights.

The last figure is the one founders overestimate. In most Indian cities the monsoon removes two or three months. Peak summer afternoons are too hot to sit outside without shade and fans. Our guide on seating capacity and covers shows how to fold those figures into a revenue plan.
Design for heat, rain and service

An outdoor area works when the staff can serve it quickly and guests stay comfortable. Keep it within easy reach of the bar so beer does not warm up on the walk. A pint poured at 4 °C on a 32 °C evening loses its chill fast. Covered or shaded seating, fans or misting where allowed and a plan for sudden rain all decide whether the area is used.

Plan how you will clear the space at closing time. Stackable furniture, lockable storage and lighting that meets any local restrictions matter more than the design render suggests.

Outdoor seating brings voices, music and smokers closer to the people who live nearby. Under India's noise rules, residential areas have lower permitted levels than commercial ones. Night limits are also stricter than day limits. Even if music stays indoors, a full terrace at 11 pm carries.

Agree a cut-off time for outdoor service that is earlier than indoor closing. Keep speakers inside. Talk to neighbours before you open, not after the first complaint. An objection from a resident can slow or stop the permission you are applying for.
Run the outdoor area as part of the venue

Once the permission is in hand, the outdoor area has to be run within its conditions every night. That means sticking to the approved seat count and boundary, closing outdoor service at the agreed time and keeping exits clear of stacked chairs. A busy Saturday is when staff are most tempted to add two extra tables on the pavement. That is also when an inspector or a neighbour is most likely to notice.

Train the floor team on the rules, not only the menu. Write the closing time and seat limit on the shift briefing sheet. Make one person on each shift responsible for the outdoor area, including checking that no drinks leave the licensed boundary. Guests walking out to the car park with a pint is a common way for a venue to breach its licence without meaning to.

Track outdoor sales separately in the POS for the first season. After a few months you will know what the area really earns on weeknights, weekends and in the shoulder months either side of the monsoon. That figure tells you whether to invest in better shade, heaters for a northern winter or nothing more at all.
Put the request in writing, with drawings

Applications move faster with a clean drawing of the outdoor area, seat count, exits, bar access and the boundary of the licensed premises. Keep copies of every approval at the venue. Inspectors will ask. A staff member on a Saturday night needs to know where the paperwork is.

Outdoor seating is one of many decisions where licensing, layout and revenue meet. The Brewery Business Management course covers all three, so you can judge whether the terrace pays before you apply for it.
faqs: Can a brewpub serve beer outdoors in India?
It depends on the state and on whether the outdoor area is included in the approved licensed premises. Check the current rules with a licensing consultant.
Which permissions are needed for outdoor seating?
Usually excise approval for the change to the licensed area, plus municipal, fire and landlord consent depending on the site.
It can be, if the area is usable for enough nights a year. Count covers, turns and real average spend, then subtract monsoon and peak heat months.
